atlas-ru.0053: HeadHunter publishes a national ranking of 411 universities by employer demand for their graduates, built on more than 500,000 graduate CVs, so the school is something employers measure. This is our reading of that ranking.
atlas-ru.0054: Yandex lets interns combine the placement with study and employs them under the Labor Code; we found no formal dual-degree system.
atlas-ru.0055: We did not establish the public sector’s weight as a graduate employer: the federal civil-service portal refused our connection. This is our reading.
atlas-ru.0056: Hiring a non-citizen runs through an annual quota and a work permit unless the post is on the ministry’s out-of-quota list; for EU and UK passport holders the UK and the US advise against travel and EU sanctions limit dealings with many Russian firms. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-ru.0057: hh.ru advises adding a professional, neutral portrait photo to the resume, first in its recommended order with the contacts.
atlas-ru.0058: hh.ru sets no page limit but asks for short, simple sentences and five to ten key tasks per job; for a new graduate one page is our reading.
atlas-ru.0059: The hh.ru resume form and the internship flows read (Yandex, Sber) use an application, a test and interviews, with no cover letter mentioned. This is our reading.
atlas-ru.0060: None of the pages read asks for references with the application. This is our reading.
atlas-ru.0061: For a foreign hire the library’s visa guide requires an apostille on the original and a Russian-notarised translation of documents such as degrees.
atlas-ru.0062: hh.ru’s resume form puts the desired salary second, after the photo and contacts, and advises setting it 15–20% above current pay and in line with the market.
atlas-ru.0063: A foreign employee needs a biometric registration and medical screening after 90 days, and the employer must hold a work permit; we found nothing on routine reference checks for graduates.
atlas-ru.0064: Job boards, internships and university fairs take open applications, while smaller firms may lean on introductions. This is our reading.
atlas-ru.0065: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Russia and the US rates it Level 4, do not travel; Yandex’s internship offers remote work only for some directions, and a foreign hire needs a permit and a visa through a consulate. This is our reading.
atlas-ru.0066: Russian for nearly all roles: the job boards, university career pages and employer programme pages read are in Russian.
atlas-ru.0067: Yandex: choose a direction and apply online, then a test task, professional interviews and meetings with hiring teams; Sber’s School 21 route has four steps: questionnaire, testing, distribution across teams and formalisation of employment.
atlas-ru.0068: University fairs add express interviews on the day (MISIS, 30 March 2026). We did not establish the usual time from application to offer, dress norms or assessment-centre use.
atlas-ru.0069: Yandex employs interns under the Labor Code and gives them a laptop, a workspace and a mentor; Sber hires interns on a temporary employment contract for three to six months.
atlas-ru.0070: CXC Global says the standard working week is 40 hours, open-ended contracts are the default and a fixed-term contract must be justified in writing, resigning employees generally give two weeks’ notice and salaries are paid at least twice a month.
atlas-ru.0071: We did not establish probation length, whether graduates negotiate, thirteenth-month practice or how long employers give to decide.
atlas-ru.0072: Hiring a non-citizen needs an annual quota application to the labour ministry by 1 July of the previous year, a vacancy published for at least 30 days at the employment centre, an employer permit, a personal work permit and an invitation; highly qualified specialists are outside the quota.
atlas-ru.0073: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Russia (updated 18 September 2026) and the US rates Russia Level 4; the EU’s 21st sanctions package of 23 July 2026 adds to rules that bind everyone under EU jurisdiction, including bans on providing certain business, legal, IT and other services. Check any offer against sanctions with a qualified adviser first.
atlas-ru.0074: We found no page on which employers sponsor foreign graduates or what they want to hear.
atlas-ru.0075: Job boards: hh.ru (with its section for young specialists) and SuperJob (Start of Career section, students.superjob.ru).
atlas-ru.0076: Employer programmes: Yandex internships, Sber’s School 21 internship, and the project career schools run with HSE by Avito and Yandex Cloud.
atlas-ru.0077: University services and fairs: HSE’s Career Development Centre (career.hse.ru) and MISIS’s spring job fair.
atlas-ru.0078: Treating sanctions and the travel advice as a footnote: the UK and the US advise against travel, and EU sanctions bind EU persons whatever the employer says.
atlas-ru.0079: Sending foreign documents as they are: they need an apostille and a Russian-notarised translation; translations sworn in Europe have no legal value in Russia.
atlas-ru.0080: Assuming English will do: the boards, university career pages and employer programme pages read are in Russian.
atlas-ru.0081: Skipping the salary field: hh.ru’s resume form asks for the desired salary and advises market-level figures.
atlas-ru.0082: The business-facing pages read (hh.ru, HSE’s career centre, MISIS’s fair) are in Russian and state no English requirement; we found no listing for a business role in English.
atlas-ru.0083: Yandex’s internship announcement and Sber’s internship page are in Russian; Yandex lists offices in Minsk and Tashkent among its internship cities, but we did not read an English requirement.
atlas-ru.0084: Sber’s internship page is in Russian and describes roles in IT directions; we found no page on English-language finance hiring.
atlas-ru.0085: We found no current graduate employment or unemployment rate for Russia: Rosstat’s pages could not be read. Yandex says 54% of its 2024 interns moved to full-time posts, and HeadHunter’s 2022 ranking of 411 universities rests on more than 500,000 graduate CVs.
atlas-ru.0087: The university requests an invitation from the Interior Ministry; you then get a 90-day study visa. Full-time students can switch to the RVPO permit, valid for the whole course plus 180 days, with a multi-entry visa and public health cover.
atlas-ru.0088: Full-time students may work in their free time with no work permit.
atlas-ru.0089: Erasmus+ links with Russian universities are suspended: only direct agreements between universities, or enrolling on your own, remain.
atlas-ru.0090: visa €80 + €30 centre; invitation 8,000 RUB; RVPO 8,000 RUB
atlas-ru.0091: There is no internship visa. Students enrolled in Russia are covered; others can come only through a university traineeship on a study visa, or be hired as ordinary or highly qualified employees. An internship on a business or tourist visa means expulsion.
atlas-ru.0093: The RVPO stays valid 180 days after graduating, with the right to work. RVPO holders can apply for a permanent residence permit within three years of graduating, honours graduates at once; other graduates get a temporary permit outside the quota.
atlas-ru.0096: Outside the quota, with no employer pre-approval and no Russian-language exam: a three-year multi-entry work visa and permit. After two years, a permanent residence permit for you and your family.
atlas-ru.0097: From 1 March 2027 the floor becomes 717,000 RUB a month, or 358,500 for teachers, doctors, researchers and some IT firms.
atlas-ru.0101: Pay below the threshold in any quarter, even through sick leave, and the status ends.
atlas-ru.0102: Ordinary hiring goes through yearly quotas the employer requests by 1 July of the year before, with 30 days of advertising; then a 90-day work visa becomes a one-year one in Russia.
atlas-ru.0104: employer 15,000 RUB; permit 5,000 RUB; invitation 8,000 RUB
atlas-ru.0106: Teachers and researchers invited by accredited universities or institutes need no work permit and no quota; from 83,500 RUB a month the host can use the three-year HQS route.
atlas-ru.0107: Short scientific visits use a humanitarian visa: at most 90 days in any 180, with no Russian salary.
atlas-ru.0108: Full-time PhD students get the RVPO for the whole programme plus 180 days, and may teach without a work permit.
atlas-ru.0109: Russia has no working-holiday agreements; casual work on a short visa leads to expulsion and a five-year ban.
atlas-ru.0111: EU citizens can get a single-entry e-visa: up to 30 days, used within 120 days of issue, not extendable or convertible. British citizens are excluded and need a paper visa with a tour operator’s confirmation.
atlas-ru.0112: A business visa runs up to a year, at most 90 days in any 180.
atlas-ru.0117: EU countries and the UK are on Russia’s list of “unfriendly” states: visa fees are four times higher and consulates can take up to 8 weeks.
atlas-ru.0118: Apostille documents at home, but have them translated with a notarised translation made in Russia: sworn translations from European courts have no legal value there.
atlas-ru.0119: European Visa, Mastercard and Amex cards do not work, and taking more than USD 10,000 in foreign currency out of Russia is a criminal offence.
atlas-ru.0120: You must be registered with the migration authorities within 7 working days. Most private landlords refuse to register tenants, and registrations bought online are a crime: stay in an accredited hotel or residence for the first weeks.
